article_title: Impact of Using Joint Productive Activity Approach on Second Language Learners' Performance in Reading Comprehension at the Basic Education Level in Nigeria
citation: Hanna Onyi Yusuf. (2013). Impact Of Using Joint Productive Activity Approach On Second Language Learners' Performance In Reading Comprehension At The Basic Education Level In Nigeria. Advances in Language and Literary Studies 4(1). https://doi.org/10.7575/aiac.alls.v.4n.1p.51
title: Joint Productive Activity lesson design: teacher and students co-construct meaning through collaborative joint tasks
description: JPA is a lesson-level design in which the teacher facilitates learning through joint productive activities with students, eliciting metacognitive activity by guiding students to answers, and designs instructional activities requiring student collaboration to accomplish a joint task, such as demonstration, dramatization, miming and songs. The teacher participates in the activity as a full collaborator, organises varied groupings, and monitors and supports collaboration. In this study it was used to teach reading comprehension to second language learners over six weeks.
requirements: The teacher arranges classroom seating to accommodate individual and group needs to communicate and work jointly, and matches the demands of the activity to the time available
constraints: The article states the teacher must manage student and teacher access to materials and technology to facilitate joint productive activity
target_learners: Junior Secondary II second language learners of English at basic education level in Nigeria
target_learning_goals: reading comprehension, including literal, inferential and critical questions
examples: The experimental group was taught reading comprehension using joint productive activities for six weeks while the control group had their normal reading comprehension lessons

article_title: Impact of Using Joint Productive Activity Approach on Second Language Learners' Performance in Reading Comprehension at the Basic Education Level in Nigeria
citation: Hanna Onyi Yusuf. (2013). Impact Of Using Joint Productive Activity Approach On Second Language Learners' Performance In Reading Comprehension At The Basic Education Level In Nigeria. Advances in Language and Literary Studies 4(1). https://doi.org/10.7575/aiac.alls.v.4n.1p.51
title: Joint Productive Activity as a CREDE pedagogic method in which teacher and students co-construct meaning from a text
description: Joint Productive Activity is one of five pedagogic methods of the Center for Research on Education, Diversity and Excellence (CREDE), which the article says have proved successful over several decades across grade levels, student populations and content areas. In JPA during language arts instruction, the teacher and a small group of students co-construct meaning from a text, with the teacher as a full collaborator modelling effective reading comprehension strategies while assessing and assisting students' comprehension efforts. The article applies this framework to second language reading instruction in Nigeria.
requirements: The teacher acts as a full collaborator who models effective reading comprehension strategies while assessing and assisting students' comprehension efforts
constraints: The article reports that in prior work JPA was unrelated to self-report of ineffective achievement gains on standardized comprehension achievement, a boundary the present study does not resolve
target_learners: predominantly Latino English language learners in the cited prior work; Nigerian Junior Secondary second language learners in this study
target_learning_goals: reading comprehension and metacognitive development during language arts instruction
examples: The study tested one of the five CREDE methods, JPA, to find out if it is likely to be effective in teaching reading comprehension to second language learners at the basic education level in Nigeria
